newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-CAROLINA PANTHERS PRESIDENT MCCORMACK RETIRES.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-CAROLINA PANTHERS PRESIDENT MCCORMACK RETIRES.

text.p: Mike McCormack, the driving force in building the expansion Carolina Panthers into title contenders in just two years, announced his retirement as the team's president on Wednesday.
The 66-year-old McCormack played a key role in obtaining an NFL franchise for Carolina and oversaw the team's rapid rise to the NFC Championship Game last season.
"The success of the Panthers has been one of the most gratifying experiences of my career," McCormack said.

"Seeing the organisation, team, and stadium evolve from a dream to reality has been more fulfilling than I can express," added McCormack, who said he decided to step down in order to spend more time with his children and grandchildren.

McCormack worked with architects in the design of the football facilities at Ericsson Stadium and guided the team through its extremely successful acquisition of players by expansion draft, free agency and the college draft.
McCormack also was instrumental in bringing NFL Coach of the Year Dom Capers and NFL Executive of the Year Bill Polian to Carolina.

"It is impossible to measure the contributions of Mike in bringing the Carolina Panthers to the position we enjoy today," said team owner and founder Jerry Richardson. "We will always be indebted to him. Just his presence gave our ownership group instant credibility."
When Carolina was awarded an NFL franchise on October 26, 1993, McCormack became general manager of the Panthers and was elevated to president in January of 1994.
McCormack was a former head coach with the Baltimore Colts and Philadelphia Eagles. He also served as a coach, president and general manager of the Seattle Seahawks.
